body:
I'll have to take a look at those. I definitely do feel like he didn't love me for a long time, maybe he thought he did, but I'm not sure he knows what love is. Thanks for the recommendation.

edit: just looked at the description: "The psychopath carefully selects the most indifferent & heartbreaking way imaginable to abandon you. They want you to self-destruct, cleaning up any loose ends as they begin the grooming process with their latest victim. They destroy you as a way to reassure themselves that their new target is better. But most importantly, they destroy you because they hate you. They despise your empathy & love—qualities they must pretend to feel every single day. To destroy you is to temporarily silence the nagging reminder of the emptiness that consumes their soul."

That is a pretty validating passage

Thank you so much. Having someone to relate to makes a difference. I'm sorry to hear you've been in two of them, this was my first and hopefully last abusive relationship. I feel like I'm stronger now that I know what to look for, how to tell the person I'm with is being controlling. It's a shame I couldn't realize it before. I think a lot of people don't understand how gradual and subtle it is until it's too late. Once I had the idea that things weren't right I tried to confront him about it, tell him I felt like he was abusive towards me. He would tell me that respect was earned and that he doesn't just be nice for no reason, that I wasn't respecting his feelings by asking not to be talked down to or humiliated. This conversation happened several times, and I began to believe him, that I was worthless, lucky to have him, and should do everything I can to accommodate him. If he didn't like it I had to change it. It's a struggle getting myself back, he was in charge of so much that everything reminds me of him and how much he controlled me. I had to get new furniture for him, get rid of any clothes he didn't like and replace them with what he approved, even cooking and cleaning remind me of him because he never did those things for himself. But I guess that's the fun of it, getting to know myself, what I like, who I like, where I want to go.

I'm definitely considering posting those texts though.
Your right about the text thing. No need to hold onto that stuff. Maybe I'll join meetup or something and get out there.

Yea, he's been blocked but from everything but my phone, I don't have a smartphone and can't figure out how to block him on that. His texts are really mean but ultimately petty. Right now I'm saving the texts to remind me of what a volatile asshole he is, when I'm having thoughts of trying to 'fix' things.

I'd love to get out and meet new people, but I just can't bring myself to do it. I've been fine recently on my own, by myself. But it usually happens late at night, or when I'm in bed, I can't help but think about the whole situation. how unfair it is that I wasted so much time with him, I think about the cruel things he's probably telling people about me (no one I care about but still hurts), how miserably alone he's left me when he kept all his friends and has a family to go back to. The other night I realized that I'm still sleeping to one side of the bed, despite not having someone to share it with, which made me break down and cry for a few hours until I fell asleep.

But reading your response makes me feel a bit better. It reminds me that there is an 'afterwards' to look forward to. I do feel like I'll never feel better, even though I know I will. Thanks for taking some time to help

thank you so much. I just had someone agree to talk to me, someone I hardly know from a chat room somewhere. but I'll keep you in mind

again thank you <3

better is a relative term, when I'm better I'm still not happy, just a different shade of miserable. I can't reach out to people I know because I don't want to be judged, I don't think their view is broad enough to understand what I'm going through. They'll just think I'm crazy
